chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Suwayd al-Qalla', from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When the boy reaches ten years of age and makes a bequest of one-third of his wealth, his bequest is valid. And if he is seven years old and makes a bequest of a small amount from his wealth, his bequest is valid.
ai.seo_question: At what age can a boy make a valid will in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the graduated testamentary capacity of minors, distinguishing between a seven-year-old who may bequeath a small amount and a ten-year-old who may bequeath one-third, provided the cause is rightful. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that while full legal majority (bulugh) is not yet reached, sufficient discernment (rushd) allows for limited disposal of wealth, serving as a precursor to full financial independence.
